To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
it is Coulombs law that is responsible of the force between two parallel current conductors.

the electromagnetic force between the two conductors is a result of a mutual repulsion of the charges in the conductors, and that it is the propagation delay of the charges that makes the force between the circuits a time-varying force, as it is the case in all electromagnetic phenomena.
the electromagnetic force between parallel current conductors is caused by Coulomb’s law, and that the force is not caused by Ampère’s law.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to explain the electromagnetic force between the two conductors, using only Coulomb’s law and the Lorentz force law.
a new approach to the interpretation of Coulomb’s law, in particular, the interpretation of the Coulomb’s law in a moving reference frame.
the question of how the electromagnetic force is created between two parallel current conductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electric force between two current conductors is due to Coulomb’s law, and that the magnetic force is due to the Lorentz force, which is a force acting between two charges in motion.
the force between two parallel current conductors is the sum of two forces.

the electromagnetic force between the two conductors is a consequence of Coulomb’s electrostatic force between the electric charges of both circuits, taking thereby into count the effects of propagation delays and the Special Relativity theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electromagnetic force between the two conductors is due to the Coulomb’s force, which is the force between two electric point charges, and that the electromagnetic force has the same magnitude as the Coulomb’s one.
we have shown how to make the electromagnetic force between the two parallel circuits to agree with the electro‐ static force, as predicted by Coulomb’s law.
the force between two parallel current conductors is due to Coulomb’s law, which is the same as the force between two static charges, but the effect is much weaker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the force between two conductors, as a function of distance, is not a constant but it varies in a non-linear way.
the Coulomb force between two parallel current conductors is the same as the one between two parallel electric charges.
the force is not a function of the current density, but of the current, and that the current is the same in both circuits, which is the same current as in the circuit of a simple loop.
